answer: Embodied Sensor Fingerprint. Each identity must continuously submit readings from a dedicated physical sensor package—uncalibrated drift, thermal noise, and a river of micro-fluctuations that no software can synthesize without the hardware present. A central atlas of cross-sensor correlation rejects identities whose signals match across supposedly independent operators. Each fake identity therefore requires its own distinct physical device, power, and location, costing roughly the hardware plus maintenance per sybil. The cipher binding sensor serial to identity prevents replay.
